claims.text: The initial non-equiatomic HEAs have a disordered FCC structure.
DFT calculations can effectively tune the magnetic behavior of non-equiatomic HEAs.
DFT calculations can effectively tune the magnetocaloric behavior of non-equiatomic HEAs.
DFT can predict an optimal HEA composition for enhanced magnetocaloric properties.
DFT can predict an optimal crystal structure for enhanced magnetocaloric properties.
Composition and crystal structure act as the structural mediators of magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior.
Ab initio calculations can predict the magnetic moment of the HEA.
Ab initio calculations can predict the entropy change of the HEA.
The proposed DFT-guided approach will increase the magnetocaloric effect by 20% relative to traditional alloy-design methods.
The proposed HEA will exhibit an entropy change of 2.5 J/kg·K at 300 K.
Traditional alloy-design methods provide an entropy change of 2.1 J/kg·K at 300 K.
The relevant operating temperature range is 250–350 K.
The primary alloying-element fractions are restricted to the range 0.1–0.5.
The accuracy of the DFT predictions depends on the exchange-correlation functional.
The treatment of electron correlations can affect predicted magnetocaloric properties.
A measured entropy change below 2.0 J/kg·K at 300 K would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: An increase from 2.1 to 2.5 J/kg·K is approximately 19.0%, not exactly the stated 20%.

The falsification threshold is inconsistent with the claimed enhancement: results from 2.0 through 2.1 J/kg·K would not meet the claimed improvement over the 2.1 J/kg·K baseline but would not falsify the hypothesis under the stated rule.
